title: Support scenarios
description: Four incoming messages of the kind that actually arrive: an angry customer with a genuine fault, a request we cannot fulfil, a case that meets an escalation trigger, and one where the customer is mistaken but polite.

tasks.title: Escalation calls
tasks.description: For each situation, decide whether it escalates now.
tasks.hint: Chapter three lists four triggers. They are deliberately mechanical.

questions.questionText: A customer mentions they are considering legal action. What do you do?

options.text: Resolve it yourself first to avoid alarming anyone
Wait to see whether they raise it again

questions.questionText: Three customers report the same fault within an hour. What is this?

options.text: An incident — say so in the team channel now
Three tickets to work through in priority order

questions.questionText: Which of these outranks the others for urgency?

options.text: A paid customer who cannot receive their delivery
A customer asking forcefully for a new feature
A customer whose workaround is inconvenient

tasks.title: Draft the first reply
tasks.description: A customer's order shipped to their previous address. Write the first reply.
tasks.hint: Acknowledge, restate, commit — with a time attached.

correct_answers: i will come back to you by

correct.answer: Your order went to your old address and that is our error. I am arranging a replacement now and will come back to you by end of day with the new delivery date.

partial.answer: Sorry about that — it looks like it went to the old address. I will come back to you by tomorrow.

incorrect.answer: Apologies for any inconvenience caused. I will look into this and get back to you.
